children: CBOT grain futures are lower in early trading, ahead of the USDA's WASDE report due at noon Eastern time. The lower trade comes after gains seen this week, which some traders see as overdone. "I feel this is a function of yesterday's action being way over done to the upside as most of the strength yesterday was lead from crude oil," says Cory Bratland of AgMarket.net in a note. Traders are expecting the report to show reductions in production and yields, due to adverse weather in the latter half of the summer. Most-active corn falls 1.6%, soybeans drop 1.6%, and wheat is down 1.5%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
